title: Walk the Campuhan Ridge at first light in Ubud
description: A 2km grass ridge between two rivers, quiet before seven and unbearably hot after nine. The obvious first morning in Ubud.

title: See the Tegallalang rice terraces before the buses
description: Terraces watered by subak, a cooperative irrigation system run by temple priests since the ninth century and now World Heritage listed.

title: Get robbed by macaques in the Sacred Monkey Forest
description: Around 1,200 long-tailed macaques in a temple complex in the middle of town. They will take sunglasses, phones and anything shiny - leave it in the room.

title: Bathe in the holy springs at Tirta Empul
description: A purification ritual Balinese Hindus have performed since 962 CE. Sarong required, and the queue moves spout by spout in a set order.

title: Watch a Legong performance in Ubud Palace
description: Gamelan and masked dance in the palace courtyard nearly every evening - a living tradition rather than a tourist show, and cheap.

title: Climb Mount Batur for sunrise
description: A 2am start up an active volcano to watch the sun come up over Lombok. Local guides are effectively compulsory and the trail is enforced as such.

title: See the lake temple at Ulun Danu Beratan
description: A water temple appearing to float on Lake Beratan in the highlands, dedicated to the goddess of lakes and rivers. It is on the 50,000 rupiah note.

title: Walk between the Jatiluwih rice terraces
description: Far larger and far quieter than Tegallalang, with walking loops through working terraces rather than a viewpoint you photograph from a cafe.

title: Swim under Sekumpul Falls
description: Seven falls dropping into one gorge in north Bali, reached by several hundred steps and a river crossing. Widely rated the island's best.

title: Watch the sunrise gate at Lempuyang
description: The Gates of Heaven framing Mount Agung. The famous reflection is a mirror held under a phone by the photographer - everyone queues for hours for it anyway.

title: Snorkel the USAT Liberty wreck at Tulamben
description: A torpedoed US cargo ship pushed off the beach by the 1963 Agung eruption, now lying 30m from shore in water shallow enough to snorkel.

title: Explore the water palace at Tirta Gangga
description: Stepping stones across carp ponds in a royal water garden built in 1946, rebuilt after Agung buried it seventeen years later.

title: Watch the Kecak fire dance at Uluwatu at sunset
description: A sea temple on a 70m cliff, with a chanting circle of about seventy men performing the Ramayana as the sun goes down behind them.

title: Learn to surf the beach break at Canggu
description: Black volcanic sand, forgiving waves at Batu Bolong, and the centre of gravity for Bali's remote-working scene.

title: Surf or watch the reef break at Uluwatu
description: You paddle out through a cave in the cliff. A world-class left over shallow reef, and unforgiving of anyone who overestimates themselves.

title: Eat babi guling in a warung
description: Spit-roast suckling pig stuffed with turmeric, lemongrass and chilli - a ceremonial dish that most warungs sell out of by early afternoon.

title: Look down on Kelingking Beach from the cliff
description: A headland shaped like a dinosaur on Nusa Penida. The descent to the sand is a near-vertical scramble on bamboo rails - people are hurt on it regularly.

title: Snorkel with manta rays at Nusa Penida
description: Reef mantas visit a cleaning station here year-round. The swell can be heavy, and the boat ride out is not for anyone prone to seasickness.

title: Cycle the flat lanes of Nusa Lembongan
description: Seaweed farms, a yellow suspension bridge to Nusa Ceningan, and a fraction of the traffic of Penida next door.

title: Watch dawn break over Borobudur
description: The largest Buddhist temple on earth, built around 800 CE and abandoned for centuries under volcanic ash. Climbing to the upper terraces is now capped and guided.

title: Walk the temple complex at Prambanan
description: A ninth-century Hindu complex of towering candi, badly damaged in the 2006 earthquake and still under restoration. The Ramayana ballet runs here in the dry season.

title: See batik being drawn by hand in Yogyakarta
description: A sultanate city and the cultural centre of Java, where batik tulis is still drawn line by line with a wax pen rather than stamped.

title: Watch sunrise over Mount Bromo from Penanjakan
description: A smoking cone inside a caldera called the Sea of Sand, with Semeru erupting on the horizon behind it. A 3am jeep and genuinely cold at altitude.

title: See the blue fire at Kawah Ijen
description: Ignited sulphuric gas burning electric blue in the dark, above a turquoise acid lake. Gas masks are essential, and miners still carry 80kg of sulphur out by hand.

title: Ride to the crater rim at Tumpak Sewu
description: A 120m curtain of water in a horseshoe amphitheatre. The descent to the base is bamboo ladders and rope in permanent spray - hard, and slippery.

title: Eat your way through a Jakarta street food night
description: Nasi goreng, satay, martabak and kerak telor from carts that appear after dark, in a city of ten million with a food scene drawn from every island.

title: Look into the crater lake at Kawah Putih
description: A pale turquoise sulphur lake in a crater above Bandung, sitting at 2,400m so the air is cool and faintly acidic.

title: Track Komodo dragons on Rinca
description: The largest lizard on earth at up to 3m, found wild on five islands and nowhere else. Rangers carry forked sticks, which is less reassuring in person.

title: Climb Padar Island for the three-bay view
description: About 800 steps to a ridge overlooking three crescent bays, each with differently coloured sand. The most photographed view in eastern Indonesia.

title: Snorkel the pink sand at Komodo
description: Red organ-pipe coral fragments mixed through white sand give the colour - one of only a handful of genuinely pink beaches anywhere.

title: See the three coloured lakes of Kelimutu
description: Three crater lakes that independently change colour - red, green, black, turquoise - as their mineral chemistry shifts. Local belief holds they receive the dead.

title: Climb Mount Rinjani to the crater rim
description: 3,726m, usually done over three days with porters, to a crater holding a lake and a new cone growing inside it. Genuinely hard, and closed in the wet.

title: Snorkel with turtles off Gili Trawangan
description: Three car-free islands where transport is bicycle or horse cart, with green turtles grazing in water shallow enough to snorkel from the beach.

title: Surf the point at Kuta Lombok
description: A string of horseshoe bays with reef breaks for every level, and a fraction of Bali's crowds despite the airport being twenty minutes away.

title: Dive Raja Ampat, the richest reef on earth
description: Surveys record over 1,500 fish and 550 coral species - the highest marine biodiversity ever measured. Getting there takes two flights and a boat.

title: Climb Piaynemo for the karst lagoon view
description: A boardwalk and 320 steps to a platform above a scatter of mushroom-shaped karst islets - the view that defines Raja Ampat in photographs.

title: Dive the wall at Bunaken
description: A vertical coral wall dropping to well over 1,000m, with visibility routinely past 30m and turtles at almost every depth.

title: Muck dive the Lembeh Strait
description: Black volcanic sand rather than coral, and the best critter diving in the world - mimic octopus, hairy frogfish, blue-ringed octopus, all on one dive.

title: Attend a Torajan funeral ceremony
description: Funerals here last days and can happen years after death, with the deceased kept at home in the meantime. Visitors are genuinely welcomed - bring a gift and a guide.

title: Trek to see orangutans at Bukit Lawang
description: Sumatran orangutans in the wild on the edge of Gunung Leuser - one of only two places on earth where the species survives, and it is critically endangered.

title: Stay on Samosir Island in Lake Toba
description: The largest volcanic lake on earth, filling a caldera left by an eruption 74,000 years ago that may have nearly wiped out early humans.

title: Surf the Mentawai Islands
description: Reeled-off perfect reef breaks reached by charter boat from Padang, and among the most consistent waves anywhere in the world.

title: Island-hop the Karimunjawa archipelago
description: 27 islands in a marine park off Java's north coast, most uninhabited, reached by a slow ferry that puts most travellers off entirely.
